message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest players in NBA history. He was born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio. James played high school basketball at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he gained national attention and was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year.

He entered the NBA directly from high school, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft. James quickly became a dominant force in the league, earning NBA Rookie of the Year honors in his debut season. Over his career, he has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat, and Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020), earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013), and has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams and NBA All‑Star games.

Beyond his on‑court achievements, James is known for his philanthropy, notably through the LeBron James Family Foundation, which focuses on education initiatives such as the “I PROMISE School” in Akron. He has also pursued business ventures, including ownership stakes in media companies and endorsements with major brands. James remains a prominent figure in sports and popular culture, recognized for both his athletic excellence and his influence off the court.
